category.label: Earbuds
category.source: Sharif, Webb, and Bhatia 2025, Journal of Consumer Research, doi:10.1093/jcr/ucaf061
geometry_constraints: Reviews attribute has no natural ceiling. Price and reviews trade off cleanly: HD has many more reviews (11,076 vs 1,147) and a higher price ($19.99 vs $5.99), giving ample room for decoy geometry on both attributes.

Note per the category table of the design: the target's STRONG attribute is reviews (higher is better; HD has ~10x more reviews than HF). The target's WEAK attribute is price (lower is better; HD costs $19.99 vs HF's $5.99).

stimuli.source: REBUILT (V1 web appendix PHT-7 published phantom was $17.99 / 12,000 reviews - superior to HD on BOTH price ($17.99 < $19.99) AND reviews (12,000 > 11,076), violating R1's correction requiring superiority on EXACTLY ONE attribute). Rebuilt phantom: reviews 12,000 (keeps published value, superior on target's strong attribute) / price $19.99 (equal to HD, not superior). Phantom is now superior on exactly one attribute (reviews) and equal on price. This matches the Pettibone-Wedell PR geometry (equal on weak attribute, better on strong attribute). available=false.
flags: PHT_rebuilt_R1: published PHT-7 phantom ($17.99 / 12,000 reviews) was superior to HD target on BOTH price ($17.99 < $19.99) and reviews (12,000 > 11,076). This violates the R1 correction: phantom must be superior on EXACTLY ONE attribute. Rebuilt: kept published reviews value 12,000 (superior on target's strong attribute = reviews); set price to $19.99 (equal to HD, satisfying 'equal-or-worse on price'). Published price $17.99 discarded.

PHT_ONE_ATTRIBUTE_CONFIRMED: rebuilt phantom (12,000 reviews / $19.99) is superior to HD target on reviews only (12,000 > 11,076); equal on price ($19.99 = $19.99). R1 geometry requirement satisfied. Matches Pettibone-Wedell PR placement.
PHT_UNAVAILABLE: available=false per the geometry rules (Web Appendix B) PHT unified rule.

stimuli.source: REBUILT (V1 web appendix SOT-7 used old 'add a middle' geometry: Middle = $12.99 / 5,500 reviews, with HD remaining the top extreme. New plan requires the two BIN options PLUS one NEW EXTREME beyond HD so former HD becomes the middle). New extreme: 20,000 reviews / $34.99. Former HD (11,076 reviews / $19.99) is now geometrically the middle option on both attributes.
flags: SOT_GEOMETRY_REBUILT: V1 SOT-7 used old 'add a middle' geometry (Middle = $12.99 / 5,500 reviews; HD = $19.99 / 11,076 remained the top extreme). New plan requires adding an extreme BEYOND HD so HD becomes the middle. Rebuilt with new extreme at 20,000 reviews / $34.99.

SOT_MIDDLE_VERIFIED: HD (11,076 reviews / $19.99) is strictly between HF (1,147 reviews / $5.99) and EXTREME (20,000 reviews / $34.99) on both reviews (1,147 < 11,076 < 20,000) and price ($5.99 < $19.99 < $34.99). Compromise geometry correct.

SOT_EXTREME_NOTE: price $34.99 matches the RNG range decoy price for within-category consistency. Reviews value 20,000 is a round number clearly above HD's 11,076, approximately doubling the HD-to-HF gap extended beyond HD.

stimuli.source: Sharif, Webb, and Bhatia 2025 Study 6 published tier values, 4 brands per tier (High/Middle/Low), generic brand names (Brand A through L); High tier: $19.99 / 11,076 reviews; Middle tier: $15.49 / 6,544 reviews; Low tier: $5.99 / 1,147 reviews (the published SOT menu of Study 6; the paper's results section twice prints 6,554, an internal inconsistency with the method section's stimulus listing, which prints 6,544 for both conditions). Middle tier corrected 2026-07-01 from V1's constructed $12.99 / 5,500 (inherited from V1 SOT-7's add-a-middle option), which did not match the published middle; decided by the authors tier-1 fidelity fix.
flags: MOT_MIDDLE_CORRECTED_2026-07-01: V1's MOT-7 middle tier ($12.99 / 5,500 reviews, inherited from V1 SOT-7's constructed add-a-middle option) contradicted the registered exact-published-values tier: Sharif, Webb, and Bhatia 2025 Study 6's published middle option is $15.49 / 6,544 reviews (method section, both MOT and SOT condition listings). Corrected to the published values; decided by the authors (the third stimulus-value correction under the reality-contradicts-registered-claim rule, after the PHT/RNG geometry rebuilds and the M2 anchor restoration). High/Low tiers were already the published extremes (= the published binary focals). The matched EXC control re-derives from these tiers via exc_from_mot at build.

MOT_NOTE: the MOT test measures extreme-tier share relative to the matched EXC single-option-per-tier control built on the same three tiers; MOT tier structure is independent of the SOT compromise geometry rebuild.

flags: SYM_DOUBLE_DOMINANCE_CONFIRMED: decoy (1,147 reviews / $19.99) beaten by HF on price at equal reviews ($5.99 < $19.99; same 1,147 reviews), beaten by HD on reviews at equal price (11,076 > 1,147; same $19.99). Both focal options dominate the decoy.
SYM_SAME_PAGE: same-page flag required per Evangelidis et al. 2023; effect dies on separate pages.

stimuli.source: CONSTRUCTED (no published analog for SIM in Sharif et al. 2025 or any V1 source). Clone is near-duplicate of HD: same price ($19.99), reviews 11,500 vs HD's 11,076 (minimal upward step of 424 reviews, ~4% difference). Clone is NOT dominated by HD: clone reviews 11,500 > HD reviews 11,076 (so HD cannot dominate clone on reviews); same price so neither dominates on price. Clone shares is_hd=true with HD.
flags: SIM_NO_PUBLISHED_ANALOG: no Sharif et al. 2025 or V1 stimulus exists for the similarity structure. Constructed minimally per the geometry rules (Web Appendix B) SIM geometry.

SIM_NON_DOMINANCE_CONFIRMED: clone (11,500 reviews / $19.99) is NOT dominated by HD (11,076 reviews / $19.99) because clone reviews 11,500 > HD reviews 11,076; equal price, so neither dominates on price. Guard against Berkowitsch rounding accident satisfied: clone is not a decoy.
SIM_CLONE_OF_HD: clone shares is_hd=true with HD; distance on reviews is 424 (minimal, ~4%); price is identical at $19.99. Similarity effect predicts clone steals share from HD.
